name: Media Optimizer
description: Inspect any media file from inside Jellyfin and convert it with FFmpeg: resolution, codec, bit depth, bitrate and audio presets, plus a genuinely lossless mode whose bit-exactness is verified by hash after every encode. Conversions run in a background queue and the original file is never modified until the result passes verification.
overview: Inspect and convert media files from inside the Jellyfin interface.

versions.changelog:
- New: moving media between drives, from Dashboard -> Move Media. It lists every library folder
with how full its drive is and how much of the library lives there, moves individual files or
a whole folder onto another drive, and says what would happen before anything does: how many
files, how much data, what would be left free and which files would be skipped and why.
- A move is a separate action from a conversion, with its own queue and its own history:
nothing is re-encoded and not a byte of the file changes. "Move to another drive..." is a
separate entry in the 3-dot menu for administrators.
- Each file is copied to a hidden staging name on the destination drive, checked against the
original by size and by hash, and only then renamed into place and the original deleted. A
failure or a cancellation before that leaves the library exactly as it was, and an original
that cannot be deleted takes the copy away again rather than leaving a duplicate. Within one
drive the file is renamed instead, which is instant.
- Artwork, .nfo files and external subtitles travel with the media file, the library entry is
repointed rather than rescanned so watched state and playlists survive, the folder layout
below the library folder is preserved, and an emptied folder is cleaned up.
- Moves pause while anyone is streaming, and a file someone is watching is never moved. The
housekeeping task now also clears partial copies left behind by a server that stopped
mid-move.

- Fixed the dialog showing a file as having no video and no audio, with a blank duration and
bitrate, and still offering to convert it. FFprobe's answer was only ever used to fill in
details on top of Jellyfin's own stream data; if Jellyfin had no record of the file, that
answer was discarded and the dialog described the file as empty. FFprobe now supplies the
whole track list when Jellyfin has nothing, and the item's own media source is tried before
either of them.
- A file whose contents genuinely cannot be read is now refused with the reason, instead of
offering "Start conversion" on a job that would map no streams and write an empty file.
- Fixed MP4 being offered for a TrueHD or Atmos remux. The container check needs the audio
track list to know MP4 cannot hold it, so with no stream data it silently passed and the
job died at the muxer.
- Dropdowns no longer cut their own labels off mid-sentence on a phone. A select clips rather
than wraps, so the labels are short now and the explanation sits underneath where it can wrap.

- Fixed the Codec dropdown being empty and every conversion being rejected with "No video
encoder was selected". When the plugin could not read FFmpeg's encoder listing it was left
with no codecs at all, and that empty result was then cached until the server was restarted.
A probe that finds nothing is no longer kept, the listing is parsed in a way that survives
FFmpeg adding a column, and FFmpeg is asked about each encoder individually as a last resort.
- The dialog now says why nothing can be re-encoded, naming the actual FFmpeg problem, instead
of showing an empty Codec dropdown and defaulting Video to "Keep exactly as it is".
- Fixed the chosen codec not reaching the server. A dropdown showing its first entry was not
the same as that entry having been selected, so a conversion could be rejected for having no
encoder while the form plainly showed one.
- A codec this server no longer provides is shown as such in the dropdown rather than being
silently swapped for a different one.

- "Try again" now works on jobs that failed before 1.4.1.0. A queued job carries the settings it
was created with, so retrying one simply replayed the container that could not hold the file.
The container is now re-checked every time a job runs, so a stale job is corrected rather than
failing the same way twice.
- Failure messages now lead with the line that names the cause. FFmpeg prints it first and then
floods its output with thread teardown, so the previous message kept the last 500 characters
and cut off the only useful sentence.
- Failures record which version of the plugin produced them.

- Fixed conversions to MP4 failing immediately on any file with text subtitles. The plan copied
the source subtitle track into MP4, which has no format for it, so FFmpeg refused to write the
file and the job died having encoded nothing. Text subtitles are now converted to MP4's own
subtitle format, and left untouched in MKV.
- Fixed MP4 being chosen for files carrying TrueHD, Blu-ray PCM or other audio MP4 cannot store.
Those now stay MKV so the track is kept exactly as it is, and the reason is shown in the dialog
instead of the container silently changing.
- Every job now runs half a second of the real encode through the real muxer before starting.
Anything FFmpeg would reject fails in a second with a readable message, rather than after hours
of encoding.
- Image-based subtitle detection now recognises DVB and XSUB tracks as well as PGS and DVD.

- Much faster, without touching the encoder. Replaced originals are now renamed in place
instead of copied to a data folder, encoding writes into the media folder so the finished
file is moved by rename, and the full decode verification that doubled every job is off by
default. On a 5 GB film that is minutes of pure disk copying removed per job.
- Hardware encoding is now tuned for quality — multi-pass, lookahead, B-frames and adaptive
quantisation — landing 10-20% larger than a slow CPU encode rather than 50%.
- New: replace and delete the original immediately, or replace and keep it for a set number of
days. Every replacement is written to replacements.log.
- Finished jobs are removed automatically after 30 days.
- The dashboard is tidier: status collapses to one line, the file picker and the history are
dropdowns, and running jobs are separated from finished ones.
- Process priority is no longer lowered by default, which was quietly slowing every encode.

- Keep only the audio and subtitle languages you actually use; everything else is removed.
This is bit-exact for the tracks you keep and is often the largest saving available. A file
is never left with no audio at all.
- Optionally remove commentary and audio-description tracks.
- The queue is now crash-safe: every change is written to disk before it is acknowledged, and
an encode interrupted by a restart or a power cut is picked up again automatically.
- Speed settings: fastest / balanced / smallest file, and a switch to use the graphics card,
which is typically ten to twenty times faster than the CPU.
- A status panel entry that measures this server's real encoding speed and names what is
slowing it down.
- Statistics: disk actually reclaimed, average reduction, and how much is still held for undo.
- Pause the queue, run a job next, cancel everything pending, and free the space held by
originals awaiting undo.
- Scrub previews are rebuilt after a file is replaced, instead of staying stale.

- Fixed the dialog's two panes rendering on top of each other. It now lives in a shadow root,
so no stylesheet on the page can reposition it.
- Fixed every default predicting a bigger file. Size is now estimated from the source's own
bitrate, and a container that mis-tags the video stream no longer skews it.
- New presets: Standard (better codec), Medium (one resolution step down), High reduction
(a step down plus a lower bitrate). The dialog opens on whichever actually helps the file.
- Removed the invented encode time. A real one appears once the server has measured itself.
- Subtitle warnings are collapsed into one line with a "Use MKV instead" button.
- Select several files on the dashboard and convert them all with one preset.
- Sort and filter the dashboard list by size, resolution, bitrate, watched state, container
and codec.
- MP4 and Replace are now the defaults; files whose subtitles MP4 cannot carry stay MKV.
- Reworded the options that were unclear.

- Conversions can now be started from the dashboard page, so the plugin is fully usable
without the in-app buttons.
- Fixed the in-app buttons never appearing: File Transformation 2.5 added admin auth to its
HTTP registration endpoint, so registration now goes through its in-process service instead.
- Added a status panel that reports each part of the plugin separately.
